mappings.note: Plain recall of an incident: why the Nawab's solitary reflection was disturbed. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because nothing here asks about Yashpal's intent or style; it is bare vishayvastu of the prescribed gadya path.
Factual detail from the narrative (which class the narrator travelled in). Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: no appreciation of mantavya or bhasha-shaili is involved.
Recall of the narrator's expectation about the compartment. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the item tests text content, not the writer's craft.
What the narrator saw on boarding -- plain bodh of the incident. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: no authorial purpose is probed.
Recall of the asantosh in the gentleman's eyes. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 since the item asks what the text reports, not what the author implies by it.

Identifies the source path and names its author -- sahityik/bibliographic identification, not comprehension of the passage. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because this frame has no biography/authorship LO, so the competency is the honest citation; C-H1.3-LO-2 rejected too as no mantavya is appreciated.
Who was already in the compartment -- character/incident recall. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: no craft question.
The safedposh gentleman's reaction to the narrator's arrival; plain content. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 as the vyangya is not what is being tested.

Resolves the referent of 'apadarth vastu' inside the passage -- a word's sense in context, which LO-1 covers. Rejected C-H1.2 because this is not a grammar category (no paryayvachi/vilom/muhavara drill).
How the Nawab's manner of eating the kheera differed -- recall of the described action. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: the item stops at what happened and does not ask what Yashpal means by it.
Reason the narrator was in second class, stated in the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because no authorial comment on class is demanded.
Where the Nawab was from -- bare fact. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: no shaili or mantavya element.
Cause of the break in the Nawab's chintan; narrative comprehension. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 as it probes the event, not the writer.
Character motivation as the text states it (being seen fancying a kheera). Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the student reports the character's feeling rather than appraising the satire on that feeling.
Why the narrator looked away -- incident-level reason given in the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: no craft appreciation.
What the idle narrator began to guess at; content recall. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 since the answer is a plot fact, not the author's purpose.
Why the narrator bought the costlier second-class ticket -- stated reasons. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: no mantavya is appraised.
What the narrator saw in the Nawab's eyes -- direct detail. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 as nothing about bhasha-shaili is asked.
Object placed on the towel (the kheeras) -- bare fact. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: no interpretive demand.
Which fact ran counter to the narrator's expectation; comprehension. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because no authorial stance is involved.

Asks what the WRITER is signalling by choosing the word 'safedposh' -- diction and implication, i.e. bhasha-shaili. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because the answer is not the dictionary sense of the word (that is the separate item 'safedposh ka arth hai') but the connotation Yashpal loads it with.
What the narrator speculated about; all options are plot content. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: the satire is not the object of the question.
The narrator's habit of constant thinking -- character detail. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 as no craft appreciation is required.
Why the narrator watched the Nawab out of the corner of his eye -- incident-level reason. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: content only. (Printed key looks doubtful; mapped on the question, not the key.)
The words with which the narrator declined the kheera -- direct recall. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because no style judgement is asked.
How the Nawab looked at the slices (satrishna aankhon se) -- text detail. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: the word is recalled, not appraised as shaili.
How he took the taste (by smelling) -- plain incident. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 since the meaning Yashpal attaches to the act is a separate item.
The narrator's own state on seeing the salted slices. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: narrative fact, no authorial intent.
Why the Nawab threw the kheera out though he did not wish to -- motive stated by the narrative. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the class-pretension reading is not what the options test.

Recall of the label the writer gave the process ('abstract', printed with a Latin artefact). Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because only the word is recalled; the item that asks what the writer MEANS by 'abstract' is mapped to LO-2 separately.
What the Nawab's belch signifies within the scene -- comprehension of the incident. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: no appraisal of the writer's irony is demanded by the options.
What the Nawab said about the kheera -- direct quotation recall. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 as no style comment is required.
Which sound indicated a full stomach (dakaar) -- bare text detail. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: content, not craft.

Resolves whom 'hum' stands for in 'hum gaur kar rahe the' -- reference resolution inside the passage. Rejected C-H1.2 because pronoun reference in context is not one of this book's vyakaran categories (sandhi/samas/vilom/paryayvachi/muhavara/vachya/pad-parichay).
What the Nawab did on looking out of the window -- incident recall. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: no mantavya is probed.
Choose the option NOT supported by the text about the smelling episode -- close reading of stated detail. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the discrimination is factual, not interpretive.

Meaning of 'satrishna' as used in the lesson -- a word's sense in context, which LO-1 names. Rejected C-H1.2 because the item is not framed as paryayvachi/vilom and tests the path's shabdarth, not grammatical usage.
Why the narrator refused the kheera (self-respect) -- character motivation in the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 since the writer's satire is not the object here.
Meaning of 'tasleem' in the lesson's Urdu-inflected vocabulary -- shabdarth in context. Rejected C-H1.2 as no grammar category (paryayvachi/muhavara) is being drilled.

The keyed answer is Yashpal's own sceptical rhetorical question about whether imagined taste can satisfy -- that reflection IS the mantavya of the piece. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because the student must pick the writer's evaluative stance, not a narrative fact.
Paraphrase of the Nawab's line about kheera being lazeez but sakeel -- meaning of a character's statement. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the aashay asked for is the speaker's, not the author's.
Explicitly asks what vyangya the writer aims at the 'nayi kahani' writers -- authorial intent and target. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because no event of the rail journey answers it.

Kriyapad identification with kriya-bhed -- a grammatical-structure task. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because the sentences are only vehicles; what is graded is grammar, not comprehension of the path. (Stem lists sentences nga-ja while the options and key carry a different set -- defect reported, mapped on the grammar intent.)

Inference about why the Nawab bought a second-class ticket, from cues in the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the answer is a character motive, not an appraisal of the writer's comment on the class.
How the narrator was looking (kankhiyon se) -- direct detail. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: no craft element.

Turns on the lesson's Urdu-Lucknowi register -- the text prints 'shukriya' where standard Hindi would put 'dhanyavad'; that is bhasha-shaili awareness. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because the item is about the writer's choice of register, not about any event or character.

Identifies what the phrase 'mamuli logon ki harkat' refers to in the passage -- referent resolution. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the student only locates the referent and is not asked to appraise the class attitude behind it.
What the narrator was observing (the method of using the kheera) -- plain content. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 as no mantavya is required.

Yes/no judgement on whether smelling can fill the stomach -- straightforward bodh of the incident. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the follow-on question about the pravritti this exposes is a separate, longer item and that one carries LO-2.
The stated effect on the narrator (gyan-chakshu khul gaye) -- narrative recall. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the item stops at the reported effect and does not ask what Yashpal builds on it.

Asks the writer's aashay in calling the method 'abstract' -- appreciation of his coinage and irony. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because the answer is not in the narrated action; it is what the writer means by the word.
Reasons for the Nawab's embarrassment about the kheera, all drawn from the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 since the options report the character's reasons rather than Yashpal's critique.
Dictionary sense of 'safedposh' -- shabdarth in context. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2, which is reserved here for the companion item asking what the WRITER signals by the same word.
What lay on the towel -- bare fact. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: no interpretive demand.

Explicitly a muhavara item ('aankhen churana'), which this book's policy files under grammatical/idiomatic usage. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because the idiom is tested as a language structure, not as an event in the path.

Asks what class the kheera is a pratik of IN THE WRITER'S VIEW -- the piece read as a comment on a class. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because no sentence of the narrative states this; it must be inferred from Yashpal's satire.
Attribution of a quoted line to its speaker (the Nawab) -- comprehension of the dialogue. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 as no style appraisal is needed.

'Gyan-chakshu khulna' is a muhavara and is graded as idiomatic usage, matching the treatment of 'aankhen churana' and 'latherh lena' in this chapter. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1 because the item does not require the episode in which the phrase occurs.
What ran counter to the narrator's expectation -- direct content. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: no craft question.
The narrator's old habit of imagining -- character detail. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because the habit is reported, not appraised.
